A1.justification: Both complete 10-page PDFs describe EchoMimicV2 and provide comparable text, equations, tables, figures, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons and component ablations in Table 2, alongside generated animation examples in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments, ablation results, and qualitative animation examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same backbone, Audio-Pose Dynamic Harmonization, Head Partial Attention, temporal-module training, and Phase-specific Denoising Loss. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanVid, curated half-body training videos, EchoMimic headshot data, EMTD evaluation, and FLUX.1-dev reference images. The represented tasks and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains AnimateAnyone and MimicMotion as quantitative comparators. Figures 4–5 retain the same qualitative comparisons with those methods, Vlogger, and CyberHost; the straightforward baseline also remains.

E3.justification: The training stages and budgets, 768×768 resolution, 24-frame clips, hyperparameters, EMTD sample counts, and ten evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Sections 3.4 and 4.1.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same pose-sampling, audio-diffusion, headshot-augmentation, loss-component, and straightforward-baseline ablations. The hand-repair examples and analysis of removing hand-pose conditioning are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Table 2 retains the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Every Table 2 entry matches, including EchoMimicV2's FID of 49.33 and FVD of 598.45. The qualitative examples in Figures 3–6 and their reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), including the latent diffusion objective and phase-specific loss definitions, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about simplified half-body animation, APDH, headshot augmentation, PhD Loss, the EMTD benchmark, and superiority over existing methods.

C2.justification: The interpretations of pose redundancy, audio-motion correlation, and component benefits remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning predefined hand poses and reduced performance on non-cropped reference images.

D1.justification: The first-page project-page link is replaced by a direct GitHub code-repository link. Implementation details and code/data-release statements otherwise remain unchanged; this documents a different access route, without establishing a new release.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and all 39 references remain unchanged, preserving the same positioning relative to EchoMimic and other human-animation methods.

P1.justification: v2 adds contributor and corresponding-author annotations, removes one email address, and splits several introductory paragraphs. The scientific wording and section order remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and both tables retain their content and design. Author footnotes and text reflow change page layout; v2 also misplaces the abstract's opening word, 'Recent,' over 'Partial Attention' at the top of the right column.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and evidence are unchanged. Although v2 provides a more direct code link and clarifies author roles, it introduces a visible abstract typesetting defect where 'Recent' overlaps 'Partial Attention.' This localized readability loss slightly outweighs the limited documentation benefits.
